## Problem

Every CI job makes an avoidable network call to `raw.githubusercontent.com` before it can start; when that call fails the job fails with `##[error]fetch failed`, unrelated to the change under test. Observed 2026-08-28 on the `pip-audit` job of run 33214025855, dead after 21 seconds, in three consecutive lines: `Could not determine uv version from uv.toml or pyproject.toml. Falling back ...` / `Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh ...` / `##[error]fetch failed`.

## Root cause

`astral-sh/setup-uv` is correctly SHA-pinned everywhere (`ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d  # v10.0.0`), but **uv itself is not pinned**: no `version:` input at any call site, no `[tool.uv] required-version`, no `uv.toml`.

Read from the pinned action's own source at that SHA (full extract in a ticket comment):

- `src/version/version-request-resolver.ts` — `WorkspaceVersionResolver.resolve` scans `getWorkspaceCandidates()`, exactly `<working-directory>/uv.toml` then `pyproject.toml`; when neither yields a specifier it logs the observed fallback line and `LatestVersionResolver` supplies `"latest"`.
- `src/version/resolve.ts` — `LatestVersionResolver.resolve` calls `getLatestVersion(manifestUrl)`: that is the fetch. `ExactVersionResolver.resolve` returns immediately and is ordered **first** in `CONCRETE_VERSION_RESOLVERS`, so an exact version never reaches the network.
- `src/version/file-parser.ts` — the `pyproject.toml` parser reads `pyproject.tool?.uv?.["required-version"]`.
- `src/version/specifier.ts` — `normalizeVersionSpecifier` strips a leading `==`, then `parseVersionSpecifier` classifies via `tc.isExplicitVersion`. `"==0.12.7"` becomes `kind: "exact"` (no network); `">=0.12.7"` becomes `kind: "range"` and **still fetches**. Only an exact `==` pin removes the fetch.

There are **25** call sites, not 8 (`grep -rn "setup-uv@" .github/workflows/`), across 12 workflow files. **None** sets `working-directory`, so all resolve against the repository root, and every one is preceded in its job by a checkout (24 `actions/checkout`, plus `gerrit-verify.yaml:178` via `lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action`). One root-level pin therefore reaches all 25 with no call-site edits.

`release.yml` is a call site, so this is also a supply-chain surface on the publishing path: the resolved uv can change between runs with no repository change. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` already pins `acli` by version and sha256 with "Never run `latest` in CI."

## Approach

Add `[tool.uv] required-version = "==0.12.7"` to the root `pyproject.toml`, plus a guard keeping it the single source.

**Why `pyproject.toml`.** It is the only already-committed file the action's zero-input workspace scan reads. A new `.github/uv-version.txt` — sibling of `.github/python-version.txt` — would need a `version-file:` input at all 25 sites, the duplication the third acceptance criterion exists to prevent. `uv.toml` is also read, but rejected: uv treats it as a *replacement* for `[tool.uv]` in `pyproject.toml`, silently orphaning any future `[tool.uv]` setting.

**Why `0.12.7`.** It is what CI resolves to today, so the pin is a no-op for CI behavior rather than a silent up/downgrade. From run 33225196631, job `build-and-test / lint + type-check`, 2026-08-29T01:08:42-43Z: `Downloading uv from ".../download/0.12.7/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"` then `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7`. The same value appears in `sweep (py3.14)`, `(py3.15)`, `(py3.14t)` and `(macos, full suite)` of that run, so it holds across the matrix.

**Accepted consequence.** `required-version` is read by uv itself, so a contributor on a different uv gets a hard error naming the fix (verified locally against uv 0.7.18: `error: Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.7.18. Update uv by running uv self update 0.12.7`). Taken as a benefit: local 0.7.18 against CI's 0.12.7 is the silent divergence `uv sync --locked` exists to prevent, and the pin makes it loud and one-command fixable. `docs/local-dev-env.md` gains a note so the error is expected.

**The guard.** The one realistic regression path is a later change adding a `version:`/`version-file:` input at one call site, which `ExplicitInputVersionResolver` honours **ahead of** the workspace scan, silently diverging that job. `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` asserts: (1) `[tool.uv] required-version` exists and is an exact `==X.Y.Z`, not a range; (2) no `setup-uv` step in `.github/workflows/**` carries `version:` or `version-file:`; (3) no root `uv.toml`. Wired into `make lint` beside the existing `check_shellcheck.py` / `check_templatefile_escapes.py` gates, so it runs offline with no CI provider required and CI inherits it through that same step.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — add `[tool.uv]` with `required-version = "==0.12.7"` and a comment on why `==` is load-bearing.
- `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` — new guard (three assertions above).
- `Makefile` — invoke the guard from `lint`.
- `tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` — new; guard passes on the real tree, fails on each skew.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — the pin and the `uv self update` remedy.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — one entry.

No `.github/workflows/**` file changes: fixing all 25 sites without editing any is the point of the mechanism. The `setup-uv` SHA pins are untouched.

## Testing

**Guard unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py`), each building a temporary tree and invoking the checker, so failure modes are proven not asserted:

- Happy path: exit 0 against this repository's real root.
- Skew, workflow: a `setup-uv` step carrying `version: "0.11.0"` makes it exit non-zero and name that file. This is the "prove the check FAILS when one site is skewed" requirement; without it the guard could only ever pass.
- Skew, range: `required-version = ">=0.12.7"` exits non-zero (a range still fetches the manifest, per `parseVersionSpecifier`).
- Skew, absent: no `[tool.uv] required-version` exits non-zero.
- Skew, shadow: a root `uv.toml` exits non-zero.

**Real-CI-log verification, anchored.** A zero-match grep proves nothing — an empty log, a skipped step, or a job that never reached setup all give zero matches. So against the Gerrit Verified run for this change (`gh run view <id> --log`), in order: first assert the **anchor** `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7` is PRESENT (emitted only after uv is actually installed, so it proves the step ran, and its value proves installed == pin — a separate claim from "the message disappeared"); only then assert `Could not determine uv version` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` are ABSENT. The action's positive line `Found version for uv in <path>: 0.12.7` (`file-parser.ts`) is recorded as corroboration. All results are pasted verbatim into a ticket comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pyproject.toml` pins uv exactly; checked by `grep -qF 'required-version = "==0.12.7"' pyproject.toml` exiting 0.
- [x] No workflow file is modified; checked by `[ -z "$(git diff --name-only origin/main -- .github/workflows)" ]` exiting 0.
- [x] The guard passes on this tree; checked by `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` exiting 0.
- [x] The guard FAILS on each of the four skews; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` exiting 0.
- [x] `make lint` runs the guard; checked by `grep -qE '^\s*python scripts/check_uv_pin\.py$' Makefile` exiting 0 and `make lint` exiting 0.
- [x] A real CI log for this change contains the anchor; checked by `gh run view <id> --log | grep -qF 'Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7'` exiting 0.
- [ ] That same CI log shows no fallback; checked by `gh run view <id> --log | grep -qF 'Could not determine uv version'` exiting NON-zero, and the same for `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
- [x] Upgrading uv is a one-line change; checked by `[ "$(grep -rlF '0.12.7' pyproject.toml Makefile scripts/check_uv_pin.py | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]` exiting 0.
